Q3587542.label: 1959 French Senate election
Q3587542.summary: The first senatorial elections of the Fifth Republic were held in France on April 26, 1959.

Q7658966.label: Swiss military referendum, 1940
Q7658966.summary: A referendum on the military was held in Switzerland on 1 December 1940. Voters were asked whether they approved of amending articles 103 and 104 of the federal law that detailed the organisation of the Swiss military. The proposal was rejected by 55.7% of voters.

Q138198.label: Spanish Socialist Workers' Party
Q138198.summary: The Spanish Socialist Workers' Party is a social democratic political party in Spain. The PSOE has been in government longer than any other political party in modern democratic Spain: from 1982 to 1996 under Felipe González, 2004 to 2011 under José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, and since 2018 under Pedro Sánchez.

mentions.c: Party of José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero (Spain, 2004–2011)

Q111181270.label: 2024 Portuguese legislative election
Q111181270.summary: A snap legislative election was held on 10 March 2024 to elect members of the Assembly of the Republic to the 16th Legislature of Portugal. All 230 seats to the Assembly of the Republic were up for election.

Q2518.desc: Chancellor of West Germany and reunified Germany (1982–1998)
Q2518.summary: Helmut Josef Michael Kohl was a German politician who served as chancellor of Germany from 1982 to 1998. He was leader of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) from 1973 to 1998 and oversaw the end of the Cold War, German reunification, and the creation of the European Union (EU).

Q11734.label: Engelbert Dollfuss
Q11734.desc: Austrian Christian Social and Patriotic Front statesman (1892-1934)
Q11734.summary: Engelbert Dollfuss was an Austrian politician and dictator who served as chancellor of Austria between 1932 and 1934. Having served as Minister for Forests and Agriculture, he ascended to Federal Chancellor in 1932 in the midst of a crisis for the conservative and nationalist government. This crisis culminated in the self-elimination of the Austrian Parliament, a coup sparked by the resignation of the presiding officers of the National Council.

Positions held: Federal Minister of Foreign Affairs of Austria

Q18119638.label: Guerrino Zanotti
Q18119638.summary: Guerrino Zanotti is a Sammarinese politician who served as a Captain Regent with Gianfranco Terenzi, from October 2014 to April 2015. He is also a member of the Grand and General Council. Zanotti has been a member of the Party of Socialists and Democrats since it was formed in 2005. He is married and has two sons. In 2016, Zanotti was re-elected to the Grand and General Council, and he became the Secretary of State for Internal Affairs.

Q526294.label: Slovenian Democratic Party
Q526294.summary: The Slovenian Democratic Party, formerly the Social Democratic Party of Slovenia, is a centre-right to right-wing parliamentary party; it is also one of the largest parties in Slovenia, with approximately 30,000 reported members in 2013.

Q182230.label: Vasile Tarlev
Q182230.summary: Vasile Tarlev is a Moldovan politician who served as the 6th Prime Minister of Moldova from 2001 to 2008.

Q23022550.label: 2016 Moldovan presidential election
Q23022550.summary: Presidential elections were held in Moldova on 30 October 2016. They were the first direct presidential elections since 1996 and followed a declaration by the Constitutional Court on 4 March 2016 that the 2000 constitutional revision that led to the president being indirectly elected by Parliament was unconstitutional.

Q391126.label: Lithuanian nuclear power referendum
Q391126.summary: An advisory referendum on the construction of a new nuclear power station was held in Lithuania on 14 October 2012, alongside parliamentary elections. The proposal was rejected by 65% of voters.

Q50667990.label: assassination of Marielle Franco
Q50667990.summary: Marielle Franco, a Brazilian politician and activist, was fatally shot on 14 March 2018, in Estácio, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The assassins were in a car that pulled up alongside the Rio de Janeiro councilwoman's car and fired several shots, which also killed the driver, Anderson Gomes.

mentions.c: Brazil: Assassination: assassination of Marielle Franco

Q114492886.label: 2022 Crimean Bridge explosion
Q114492886.desc: explosion on the Crimean Bridge that occurred on 8 October 2022
Q114492886.summary: The 2022 Crimean Bridge explosion occurred on 8 October 2022, at 6:07 a.m. A fire broke out on the Crimean Bridge as a result of an explosion of a bomb that had been loaded onto a truck. The explosion occurred on the road bridge, on the westbound vehicle lanes, from Russia to Kerch in Russian-occupied Crimea.

Q4871126.label: Battle of Goodenough Island
Q4871126.desc: 1942 Pacific battle of World War II
Q4871126.img: Australian soldiers with Japanese flag captured at Goodenough Island.jpg
Q4871126.summary: The Battle of Goodenough Island, also known as Operation Drake, was a battle of the Pacific campaign of World War II. The Allies landed on Goodenough Island, Papua, and clashed with a Japanese Kaigun Rikusentai. The Japanese troops had been stranded on the island during the Battle of Milne Bay in late August 1942. "Drake Force", consisting of the Australian 2/12th Battalion and attachments, landed on the southern tip of Goodenough Island at Mud Bay and Taleba Bay on 22 October, tasked with denying the Japanese use of the island prior to the Buna campaign.

Q12406742.label: New Britain campaign
Q12406742.desc: World War II campaign between Allied and Imperial Japanese forces
Q12406742.summary: The New Britain campaign was a World War II campaign fought between Allied and Imperial Japanese forces. The campaign was initiated by the Allies in late 1943 as part of a major offensive which aimed to neutralise the important Japanese base at Rabaul, the capital of New Britain, and was conducted in two phases between December 1943 and the end of the war in August 1945.

Q3139030.label: Operation Martlet
Q3139030.desc: 1944 part of a series of British attacks to capture the French town of Caen and its environs from German forces during the Battle of Normandy of World War II
Q3139030.summary: Operation Martlet was part of a series of British attacks to capture the French town of Caen and its environs from German forces during the Battle of Normandy of World War II begun by the Allies. It was a preliminary operation undertaken on 25 June 1944 by XXX Corps of the British Second Army, to capture Rauray and the area around Noyers. The attack was to protect the right flank of VIII Corps as it began Operation Epsom, an offensive into the Odon Valley west of Caen, on 26 June.

Q180182.label: Battle of Iwo Jima
Q180182.desc: 1945 major battle in which US Forces captured the island of Iwo Jima from Japan during World War II
Q180182.img: Stars and Stripes on Mount Suribachi (Iwo Jima).jpg
Q180182.summary: The Battle of Iwo Jima was a major battle in which the United States Marine Corps (USMC), United States Navy (USN), and United States Army (USA) landed on and eventually captured the island of Iwo Jima from the Imperial Japanese Army (IJA) during World War II. The American invasion, designated Operation Detachment, had the goal of capturing the island with its two airfields: South Field and Central Field.

Q710614.label: Bombing of Kure
Q710614.desc: 1945 naval battle of World War II
Q710614.wiki: Attacks on Kure and the Seto Inland Sea
Q710614.img: U.S. Navy carrier aircraft attack the Japanese battleship Haruna near Kure, Japan, on 28 July 1945 (80-G-490226).jpg
Q710614.summary: The attacks on Kure and the Inland Sea were a series of large-scale air raids by United States and British naval aircraft in late July 1945 that sank most of the surviving large warships of the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN). The United States Third Fleet's attacks on Kure Naval Arsenal and nearby ports on 24, 25, and 28 July sank an aircraft carrier, three battleships, five cruisers, and several smaller warships.

Q55138262.label: Operation Jay
Q55138262.desc: Operation jay was a us marine corps
Q55138262.summary: Operation Jay was a U.S. Marine Corps and Army of the Republic of Vietnam (ARVN) search and destroy operation on the Street Without Joy, northern Thừa Thiên Province, lasting from 25 June to 2 July 1966.

Q27997142.label: Aleppo offensive (June–July 2016)
Q27997142.summary: The Aleppo offensive refers to a military operation launched on the northern outskirts of Aleppo in late June 2016, by the Syrian Army. The aim of the offensive was to cut the last rebel supply line into Aleppo city.

Q171990.label: laissez faire
Q171990.desc: abstention by governments from interfering in the workings of the free market
Q171990.summary: Laissez-faire implies that nothing restricts what happens, irrespective of the potential consequences. In the financial area, it is a type of economic system in which transactions between private individuals are free from any form of economic interventionism.

Q568790.label: Battle of Fromelles
Q568790.desc: 1916 military operation on the Western Front during World War I
Q568790.summary: The Attack at Fromelles (French pronunciation: [fʁɔmɛl] was a military operation on the Western Front during the First World War on 19–20 July 1916. The attack was carried out by British and Australian troops and was subsidiary to the Battle of the Somme. General Headquarters of the British Expeditionary Force had ordered the First Army and Second Army to prepare attacks to support the Fourth Army on the Somme, 50 mi to the south, to exploit any weakening of the German defences opposite.

Participants: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

Q7886806.label: Unione Nazionale
Q7886806.summary: National Union was a pro-fascist Italian Catholic political party during the 1920s, the first of several "Clerico-Fascist" political organizations established within the decade. The party was established with the permission of Pope Pius XI, dealing the final blow to the anti-fascist Catholic Italian People's Party.

Q334294.label: Anatoly Sobchak
Q334294.summary: Anatoly Aleksandrovich Sobchak was a Russian politician and legal scholar, a co-author of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, and the first democratically elected mayor of Saint Petersburg.

Party: Communist Party of the Soviet Union
